answer: Someone I genuinely admire is a former teacher of mine who went far beyond what his job required. I knew him through secondary school in Sirajganj, where he taught mathematics, but his real gift was noticing students who were quietly struggling. I was one of them for a while, because I found algebra completely baffling in my first year with him. In terms of his qualities, he was endlessly [[patient]], staying behind after class to help anyone who asked, and he never made you feel foolish for not understanding. What I admired most was his [[humility]]; despite being extremely knowledgeable, he always spoke to us as equals. He had a way of making difficult ideas feel [[accessible]], often using examples from the local market or cricket scores, and he clearly cared about the person, not just the grade. Years later, I still remember specific things he said that shaped how I think. As for why I admire him, I think what sets people like him apart is that they are motivated by a genuine desire to help rather than any reward. He was never well paid, and he could easily have earned more from private coaching, but he chose to help struggling students for free instead. He left a [[lasting impression]] on hundreds of students, and I count myself lucky to have been one of them. In fact, in my own job I often try to explain things to students the way he once explained things to me.

followUps.q: Are you still in touch with him?
followUps.answer: Not regularly, but I bump into him now and then in town. He is retired now, and he always asks about my work. It is quite touching that he still remembers me after all these years.

followUps.q: Would you ever like to become a teacher?
followUps.answer: Perhaps in some form. My job already involves a lot of guiding and explaining, and I find that side of it deeply [[fulfilling]], but I am not sure I have the patience for a classroom of teenagers.

note: Changed his subject from English to mathematics so he does not clash with the English teacher in sp2_people_16; added my struggle with algebra, free help instead of coaching, link to my job; mark moved to 'lasting impression'.
